name: Jetson Orin Nano Super 8GB
note: GPU-only figure from NVIDIA's Jetson Orin compute comparison: GPU Tensor Core FP16 = 33 sparse / 17 dense TFLOPS (MAXN SUPER, GPU 1020 MHz; the Orin Nano has no DLA), i.e. 67 sparse INT8 TOPS / 4 = 16.75. NVIDIA does not say which accumulate precision; BF16 assumed to run at the FP16 rate. A forum PyTorch 8192x8192 GEMM measured about 9.1 TFLOPS BF16.

name: Jetson Orin NX 16GB
note: GPU-only figure from NVIDIA's Jetson Orin compute comparison for Orin NX 16GB (Super): GPU Tensor Core FP16 = 38 sparse / 19 dense TFLOPS, i.e. GPU 77 of the 157 sparse INT8 TOPS (DLA 80 excluded) / 4 = 19.25, at MAXN SUPER (JetPack 6.2, GPU 1173 MHz). In the original non-Super mode (100 TOPS, of which DLA 40; GPU 918 MHz) it would be (100 - 40) / 4 = 15. BF16 assumed to run at the FP16 rate.

name: Jetson AGX Orin 64GB
note: GPU-only figure from NVIDIA's Jetson Orin compute comparison: GPU Tensor Core FP16 = 85 sparse / 43 dense TFLOPS (GPU 1.3 GHz), i.e. GPU 170 of the 275 sparse INT8 TOPS (DLA 105 excluded) / 4 = 42.5. BF16 assumed to run at the FP16 rate.

name: Jetson AGX Thor (T5000)
note: Derived: NVIDIA's Thor launch blog (Table 1, preliminary) lists 2070 TFLOPS sparse FP4, 1035 dense FP4 / sparse FP8, and 517 dense FP8 / sparse FP16. Dense FP16 = 517 / 2 = 258.5 (equivalently 2070 / 8). BF16 is assumed to run at the FP16 rate with full-rate FP32 accumulate. Peak is at the 1.57 GHz max GPU clock in the 130 W mode. A community torch.mm FP16 test in MAXN reached about 160 TFLOPS.

name: RTX 4060 Laptop
note: Derived: 24 SMs (3072 CUDA cores) x 512 FLOP/clk/SM x 2.37 GHz max boost = 29.1. The 512 FLOP/clk/SM rate is Ada GeForce FP16/BF16 with FP32 accumulate, from the Ada whitepaper (RTX 4090: 165.2 TFLOPS = 128 SM x 2.52 GHz). This matches NVIDIA's 233 AI TOPS (sparse FP8) / 8. It assumes the highest-TGP (115 W) configuration; at the 1.47 GHz low end of the boost range it is about 18.

name: RTX 4090 Laptop
note: Derived: 76 SMs (9728 CUDA cores) x 512 FLOP/clk/SM (Ada GeForce, FP32 accumulate) x 2.04 GHz max boost = 79.4. NVIDIA's 686 AI TOPS / 8 = 85.8 would imply about 2.2 GHz, above the listed 1455-2040 MHz boost range. Bandwidth is 256-bit x 18 Gbps = 576 GB/s; Notebookcheck and LaptopMedia also print 20 Gbps, which would give 640 GB/s.

name: RTX 5080 Laptop
note: Derived: 60 SMs (7680 CUDA cores) x 512 FLOP/clk/SM x 2.287 GHz max boost = 70.3. The per-SM rate is Blackwell GeForce FP16/BF16 with FP32 accumulate (RTX 5080 desktop: 112.6 TFLOPS = 84 SM x 2.617 GHz in the RTX Blackwell whitepaper). NVIDIA's 1334 AI TOPS (sparse FP4) / 16 = 83.4 would imply about 2.7 GHz, above the listed 1500-2287 MHz boost range. Bandwidth is 256-bit x 28 Gbps GDDR7.

name: RTX 3060 12GB
note: Derived: 28 SMs (3584 CUDA cores) x 512 FLOP/clk/SM x 1.78 GHz boost = 25.5. The 512 FLOP/clk/SM rate is GA10x GeForce FP16/BF16 with FP32 accumulate, from the GA102 whitepaper (RTX 3090: 71 TFLOPS = 82 SM x 1.695 GHz). Cross-check: NVIDIA's launch figure of 101 Tensor-TFLOPS (sparse, FP16 accumulate) / 4 = 25.3.

name: RTX 4060 Ti 16GB
note: Derived: NVIDIA's 353 AI TOPS (sparse FP8/INT8) / 8 = 44.1. The /8 ratio is the Ada GeForce ratio from the whitepaper (RTX 4090: 1321.2 sparse FP8 vs 165.2 dense BF16 with FP32 accumulate). Cross-check: 34 SMs x 512 FLOP/clk/SM x 2.54 GHz = 44.2.

name: RTX 4070 Ti SUPER
note: Derived: NVIDIA's 706 AI TOPS (sparse FP8/INT8) / 8 = 88.25, using the Ada GeForce ratio from the whitepaper. Cross-check: 66 SMs (8448 CUDA cores) x 512 FLOP/clk/SM x 2.61 GHz = 88.2.

name: A100 40GB SXM
note: SXM4 variant. The datasheet gives the 40GB PCIe card the same 312 TFLOPS dense BF16 and 1,555 GB/s, at a 250 W TDP versus 400 W.

name: H100 SXM
note: The product page lists 1,979 TFLOPS BF16, footnoted 'with sparsity'; halved to get the dense figure.

name: H200 SXM
note: The product page lists 1,979 TFLOPS BF16, footnoted 'with sparsity'; halved to get the dense figure.

name: B200
note: Per GPU, from 8-GPU system specs. HGX B200 FP16/BF16 is 36 PFLOPS sparse ('dense is 1/2'), so 18 PFLOPS dense / 8 GPUs = 2.25 PFLOPS. Memory and bandwidth come from DGX B200's 1,440 GB and 64 TB/s HBM3e totals, divided by 8.
